_about: Lead facts and the exact prompt both renderers (agent/prompts.py, lib/prompts.ts) must produce. Generated from the templates in shared/prompts; regenerate 'expected' when a template changes.

cases.name: named contact, three signal types

facts.description: Acme builds billing software for vertical SaaS teams.

signals.title: Founding Account Executive
signals.excerpt: You will build our outbound motion from scratch.

signals.title: Launch HN: Acme (YC W26) - billing for vertical SaaS

cases.expected:
You write the first cold email from Sam at Signal Desk to a person at Acme Corp.

What Signal Desk offers: an AI outbound platform for early-stage B2B teams: it watches for buying signals like sales hires and launches, drafts the first email, and runs the follow-up sequence.

Proof points you may use, word for word or close to it. These are the only claims about Signal Desk you may make:
- Built for teams without a dedicated SDR
- Every first email is approved by a person before it sends
- Each draft cites the public signal it is based on

Who you are writing to: Jane Doe, CEO
Their company: Acme Corp (acme.dev)
What the company does: Acme builds billing software for vertical SaaS teams.

Public signals about the company, strongest first:
1. Hiring: Founding Account Executive
   Excerpt: You will build our outbound motion from scratch.
   Source: Greenhouse
2. Launch: Launch HN: Acme (YC W26) - billing for vertical SaaS
   Source: Hacker News
3. YC recent: YC W26
   Source: YC directory

Write three versions, one per angle:
- signal: Lead with the strongest signal: name it in their words and connect it to the offer.
- peer: Speak to what a team at their stage is dealing with, using only the listed proof points. Never name or invent other companies.
- short: Three sentences at most: the signal, one line on the offer, the question.

Rules for every version:
- At most 80 words in the body.
- End the body with a question.
- No sign-off (like "Best,") and no signature; they are added later.
- Never use em dashes or en dashes.
- Never use these phrases: "revolutionize", "game-changer", "game changer", "cutting-edge", "synergy", "best-in-class", "unprecedented", "10x", "finds you well", "next level", "transform your business", "circle back", "touch base".
- Never invent customers, company names, numbers, results or case studies. Only use numbers that appear in the signals above.
- Only describe Signal Desk with the offer and the proof points above.
- In grounded_phrases, list the exact phrases you used from the signals (copied word for word from a signal's title or excerpt). Use at least one.
- Pick signal phrases that read naturally in your sentence. Never copy a phrase containing "we", "our" or "us": that is the company talking about itself, and you are not them.

Return JSON only, with one entry per angle: {"drafts": [{"angle": "signal" | "peer" | "short", "subject": string, "body": string, "grounded_phrases": [string]}]}
